Advanced L2 features with basic L3 routing for both IPv4 and IPv6

Simplified VoIP deployments using the advanced Auto-QoS feature


Auto-configurable via OmniPCX Office

LLDP with MED extensions for automated device discovery

OS6560 - Power Supply 
▪Re-use existing power supplies from the OS6860 PoE family
• Modular supply provides OS6560 PoE power budget flexibility vs OS6450 fixed 
budgets/supplies
– Increase or decrease PoE budget vs fixed PoE options with the OS6450
– Allows for load sharing between supplies
• Internal modular allows for a 1RU redundant configuration vs a 2RU with the OS6450-
P24/P48
Benefits:  load sharing, flexible PoE budget offering 
and a 1RU redundant configuration
Part number
Description
OS6560-BP-P 
OS6560-BP-P modular 300W AC PoE backup power supply. Provides system and 
PoE backup power to one OS6560 24/48 PoE switch. Ships with country specific 
power cord.
OS6560-BP-PH
OS6560-BP-PH modular 600W AC PoE backup power supply. Provides system and 
PoE backup power to one OS6560 P24Z8/24 ,P24X4/P48X4,P48Z16 switch. Ships 
with country specific power cord.
OS 6560-BP-PX
OS6560-BP-PX modular 920W AC PoE backup power supply. Provides system and 
PoE backup power to one OS6560 24/48 PoE switch. Ships with country specific 
power cord.

Management Tools
Accessing the switch may be done locally or remotely
Management tools include: 
CLI
May be accessed locally via the console port, or remotely via Telnet
WebView
Which requires an HTTP client (browser) on a remote workstation
SNMP
Which requires an SNMP manager (such as Alcatel-Lucent’s OmniVista or HP OpenView) on the

<<<PAGE 139>>>
Disaster Recovery Using a USB Flash Drive
A USB flash drive can be loaded with the necessary files to recover a failed 
CMM. This can be used if the image files on the CMM become corrupted, 
deleted, or the switch is unable to boot from the CMM for other reasons
.Perform the following steps to run Disaster Recovery:
1 Create the directory structure 6900/certified and 6900/working on the USB flash 
drive with the backup system and configuration files.
2 Copy the Trescue.img file to the root directory on the USB flash drive.
3 Connect the USB flash drive to the CMM and reboot. The switch will automatically 
stop and display the option to perform a disaster recovery.
4 Enter the ‘run rescue’ command from miniboot/uboot and follow the recovery 
prompts.
Once complete, the CMM will reboot and be operational again.

<<<PAGE 140>>>
Automatically Copying Code Using a USB Flash Drive
Auto-copy
The switch can be configured to automatically mount and copy  the image files from 
the USB device to the /flash/working directory 
Create a file named aossignature in the root of the USB flash drive
Create a directory named xxxx/working* on the USB flash drive with all the proper image files
-> usb enable
-> usb auto-copy enable
Connect the USB flash drive to the CMM; the images will be validated and copied to the 
/flash/working directory of the CMM and the switch will reboot from the working directory 
applying the code upgrade
Once the switch reboots the auto-copy feature is automatically disabled to prevent another upgrade
* xxxx= switch model

<<<PAGE 141>>>
Backup Files Using a USB Flash Drive
The following is an example of how to backup the images and configuration 
from certified and running directories to an USB Flash Drive using the usb and 
usb backup admin-state commands.
-> usb enable
-> usb backup admin-state enable
-> write memory
When the write memory command is executed in this example, the 
configuration files from /flash/running-directory are copied to 
/uflash/6900/running-directory name.
When the copy running certified command and the write memory command 
with the flash-synchro option is executed, the configuration and images from 
/flash/certified are copied to /uflash/6900/certified.
Note. Back-up cannot be enabled if auto-copy is enabled and auto-copy cannot be enabled if 
back-up is

OmniSwitch 6860 - Setting the EMP IP Address
The EMP IP address is shared between both CMMs and
stored in the boot.cfg file. (Required for remote access)
The Primary or Secondary’s CMM’s IP address, stored in NVRAM. (Not required 
for remote access)
Changes stored in NVRAM will remain with the CMM if the CMM is moved to a different 
chassis.
All the EMP and CMM’s IP addresses must be in the same subnet.
Each of the IP addresses must be unique.
-> modify boot parameters

Boot > boot empmasklength 24

Boot > commit boot
Boot > exit

User Accounts 
Admin and Default
Two default user accounts
Admin
Full privileges
By default, access only allowed through console port
Cannot be modified except for password
Default password is ‘switch’
Default
Not an active user account
Default privileges given to new user
Ability to create new users with full or limited access rights
Partition Management
Limits commands a user can run
Type of access FTP, Telnet, SNMP, Console, WebView

<<<PAGE 177>>>
User Accounts
Two types of accounts: 
Network administrator accounts.
Configured with user (sometimes called functional) privileges. 
These privileges determine whether the user has read or write access to the switch 
and which command domains and families the user is authorized to execute on the 
switch.
End-user or customer login accounts.
Configured with end-user profiles rather than functional privileges. 
Profiles are configured separately and then attached to the user account. A profile 
specifies command domains to which a user has access as well as VLANs, ports.

Remote Desktop Connection 
This chapter gives you information to connect to the remote lab according to your Operating System. 
1.1. 
Windows Seven 
- Open Remote Desktop Connection 
 
 
 
- Expand Show Options then navigate to the Advanced tab

- Enter the following Parameters: 
- Connection Settings: Use this RD Gateway server settings 
- Server name: remotelab.education.al-enterprise.com  
- Logon method: Allow me to select later 
- Bypass RD gateway server for local address: Ticked 
- Logon Settings – Use my RD Gateway credentials for the remote computer: ticked 
- Click OK

<<<PAGE 193>>>
3 
R-LAB Preparation 
 
 
 
- Click back to the General tab 
- On the Computer field enter your allocated server (should be in the form LanPodX, where X is the Pod 
number) 
 
 
 
- Click on Connect 
 
 
 
- On the username field, enter your allocated username (should be in the form LanPodXa@remote-lab.com 
where X is the pod number) 
- On the password field enter your allocated password (should correspond to the session ID – 4 digits) 
- Click on OK 
- You are now connected to the remote desktop

2.2. 
Desktop 
2.2.1. 
Generalities 
- Several shortcuts are available on the desktop and will be described further. 
 
 
 
- First thing to check to get comfortable with the RLAB is the keyboard. Normally, when you first open a 
session, Remote Desktop recognizes your keyboard and applies the good layout. If the previous session was 
not properly closed (i.e. with a Log off), it may keep previous keyboard configuration.  
- Check then the keyboard layout in the taskbar : 
 
- If it’s not the correct one, the easier to fix it is to close the RDP session and re-open it. 
- Click on start then Log off and re-establish your RDP session as seen in step 1. 
 
 
 
Tips 
At the end of the training, it’s better to use the log off function instead of just leaving Remote Desktop with 
the close button (the “X” in top right corner) as in that case the session remains active on the server with all 
environment, like screen resolution, keyboard layout and open applications…

<<<PAGE 202>>>
12 
R-LAB Preparation 
 
2.2.2. 
Switch console 
- On the desktop, you’ll find 8 shortcuts to the different switches available on your pod 
 
- By double-clicking on it, you open a teraterm console 
 
Notice the banner which indicate you the switch you’re connected on. 
 
Tips 
If you get a message “Hunting Group Busy” when you open a teraterm console, it means that another teraterm 
session has already been opened.  
2.2.3. 
Vmware clients 
- On the desktop, you’ll find a shortcut to the VMware vSphere Client, allowing you to control client VMs 
 
- By double-clicking on it, you will be asked for the connection parameters 
- IP address/Name = vcenter.remote-lab.com 
- The Use Windows session credentials should be ticked so you don’t have to enter User name nor 
password. 
 
- Click Login 
- In the left side of the window, you’ll find the different virtual machines which will be used during the 
labs.

<<<PAGE 203>>>
13 
R-LAB Preparation 
 
 
- To open a virtual machine, right-click on it and select open console. 
 
- If the VM is not started, you can press the Play button 
 to start it. 
 
 
 
Tips 
All VM are configured with an English US keyboard, your current keyboard layout is not take into account. Take 
care of that when you’re typing a command.

This lab is designed to familiarize you with the code, chassis information, and NIs, including code versions and 
revision levels. 
It’s important to determine code versions and serial numbers of the CMMs and NIs in the switch. These can be 
helpful for troubleshooting when dealing with customer support or for upgrading switch hardware and software 
 
The following will show you how to gather code and module information on a switch.

Working/Running/Certified Directory 
 
 1 
Working/Certified Directory in R6 
In release 6, an OmniSwitch provides the user with the ability to keep two separate configurations as well as 
two separate versions of AOS stored on the switch. These are stored in the WORKING and CERTIFIED directories. 
The switch can boot from either configuration. The AOS files are the *.img files and the configurations are the 
boot.cfg files. 
When a switch boots the RUNNING CONFIGURATION will come from either the certified or working. 
The switch boots from the CERTIFIED directory when the WORKING and CERTIFIED directories differ. 
1.1. 
Show Currently Used Configuration 
Open a console to a R6 switch (i.e. 6450). 
Used following command to see which directory the switch booted from.  
It will show either CERTIFIED or WORKING. 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show running-directory 
 
CONFIGURATION STATUS 
   Running CMM              : PRIMARY, 
   CMM Mode                 : MONO CMM, 
   Current CMM Slot         : 1, 
   Running configuration    : WORKING, 
   Certify/Restore Status   : CERTIFIED 
SYNCHRONIZATION STATUS 
   Running Configuration    : SYNCHRONIZED, 
« Running Configuration » line display CERTIFIED or WORKING. 
In our example: 
- “Running configuration” field displays WORKING. (the switch booted from working) 
- « Certify/Restore Status » field displays CERTIFIED.(working et certified are identical) 
- «  Running Configuration «  in «  SYNCHONISATION STATUS”  field indicates SYNCHRONIZED. 
(Configuration has been saved on flash /working (boot.cfg). 
- The switch boots from the WORKING directory when the WORKING and CERTIFIED directories are identical 
(.img & boot.cfg). 
- The switch boots from the CERTIFIED directory when the WORKING and CERTIFIED directories differ. 
 
To view the code version currently used by the switch, type: 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show microcode working 
   Package           Release       Size     Description 
-----------------+---------------+--------+----------------------------------- 
KFbase.img        6.7.1.76.R04    16731363 Alcatel-Lucent Base Software 
KFos.img          6.7.1.76.R04     3554882 Alcatel-Lucent OS 
KFeni.img         6.7.1.76.R04     5974081 Alcatel-Lucent NI software 
KFsecu.img        6.7.1.76.R04      628199 Alcatel-Lucent Security Management 
KFdiag.img        6.6.4.288.R01    2329809 Alcatel-Lucent Diagnostic Software 
The command above shows the version currently used on the switch. It is also possible to insert the keywords 
"working", "certified" or "loaded" (= current configuration) at the end of the command to display the version 
of code available in these directories.

Working/Running/Certified Directory 
 
1.2. 
Where is the Switch Running From? 
When the switch boots, (depending on the switch configuration), it will load either the working or certified 
directory into RAM (running). Once it boots from one of these directories, that configuration then becomes 
the running configuration. 
Although changes made to the configuration take effect immediately, they cannot be written or saved if the 
certified directory was loaded. 
Let’s create three new VLANs 2, 3, and 99. Type the following: 
-> vlan 2 
-> vlan 3 
-> vlan 99 
-> show vlan 
                              stree                 mble   src 
 vlan  type  admin   oper   1x1   flat   auth   ip   tag   lrn   name 
-----+-----+------+------+------+------+----+-----+-----+------+---------- 
   1    std   on    off     on    on     off    on   off     on   VLAN 1 
   2    std   on    off     on    on     off   off   off     on   VLAN 2 
   3    std   on    off     on    on     off   off   off     on   VLAN 3 
  99    std   on    off     on    on     off   off   off     on   VLAN 99 
Do you remember the shortcut using the <tab> key? We could have also shortened the command by using: 
-> vlan 2-3 99 (R6) 
The above commands created three VLANs with their respective numbers. Entering the commands makes 
changes to the running Configuration. The changes take effect immediately, but have not been written 
permanently so they will be lost on a reboot.   
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show running-directory 
 
CONFIGURATION STATUS 
   Running CMM              : PRIMARY, 
   CMM Mode                 : MONO CMM, 
   Current CMM Slot         : 1, 
   Running configuration    : WORKING, 
   Certify/Restore Status   : CERTIFY NEEDED 
SYNCHRONIZATION STATUS 
   Running Configuration    : NOT SYNCHRONIZED, 
The "Running Configuration: NOT SYNCHRONIZED" line indicates that the configuration is not backed up in 
flash. 
To demonstrate this, reboot the switch. Type the following: 
-> reload working no rollback-timeout (R6) 
-> reload from working no rollback-timeout (R8) 
Confirm Activate (Y/N) : y 
This will reboot the switch, but it will now boot from the WORKING directory. The ‘no rollback-timeout’ 
parameter tells the switch to continue running under the WORKING directory permanently rather than 
rebooting after a specified amount of time. In some circumstances, such as testing a configuration change, it 
may be useful to have the switch reboot automatically after a certain number of minutes or at a specific 
date/time to force it to return to the previously certified configuration 
When the switch reboots, login and check to see which VLANs have been created. 
Type the following: 
-> show vlan 
                              stree                 mble   src 
 vlan  type  admin   oper   1x1   flat   auth   ip   tag   lrn   name 
-----+-----+------+------+------+------+----+-----+-----+------+---------- 
   1    std   on    off     on    on     off    on   off     on   VLAN 1 
 
Notice that the VLANs do not exist. This is because the changes were made to the running configuration but 
were not saved. Let’s do the same again, but this time we’ll save the changes to the working directory.

<<<PAGE 216>>>

Working/Running/Certified Directory 
 
1.3. 
Working Directory 
The working directory is a directory on the switch where the configuration file and code are stored. This 
directory can be read when the switch boots and the configuration stored in the boot.cfg file will be applied.  
If the directory does not contain a boot.cfg file, note that it will be created when the write memory 
command is issued. During the previous exercise, we did not launch this command, the configuration in 
memory was thus not stored hence the loss of configuration at restart. 
Re-create the three VLANs: 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> vlan 2 3 99 (R6) 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show vlan 
                              stree                 mble   src 
 vlan  type  admin   oper   1x1   flat   auth   ip   tag   lrn   name 
-----+-----+------+------+------+------+----+-----+-----+------+---------- 
   1    std   on    off     on    on     off    on   off     on   VLAN 1 
   2    std   on    off     on    on     off   off   off     on   VLAN 2 
   3    std   on    off     on    on     off   off   off     on   VLAN 3 
  99    std   on    off     on    on     off   off   off     on   VLAN 99 
 
The configuration file the switch reads upon boot is called boot.cfg.  The boot.cfg file can exist in either the 
working or certified directory.  
-> ls /flash/working

   Certify/Restore Status   : CERTIFY NEEDED 
SYNCHRONIZATION STATUS 
   Running Configuration    : SYNCHRONIZED, 
 
The configuration in RAM (Running Configuration) is synchronized (saved in flash in working). 
The working and certified directories are not identical (Certified needed). 
The boot.cfg file has now been created or updated (check the timestamp -> ls /flash/working). 
The command above writes the running configuration to the boot.cfg file in the working directory.  Now if 
the switch is rebooted from the working directory, the configuration changes were saved so will be loaded 
into the running directory on startup.  Let’s reboot the switch, giving it the command to reboot from the 
configuration stored in the working directory.

By using the parameter ‘no rollback-timeout’ with the reload command, the switch will permanently run 
with that configuration. The ‘rollback-timeout’ parameter could be used to have the switch automatically 
reboot after a specified amount of time.  
The following command will cause the switch to reboot to the WORKING directory, then after 1 minute 
reboot again (this is just an example, we could put an extended amount of time or a specific date/time for 
the reboot). 
-> reload working rollback-timeout 1 (R6) 
Confirm Activate (Y/N) : y 
1.4. 
Certified Directory 
Recall that the certified directory can be used to store a backup or approved configuration on the switch. 
When the switch boots, it compares the configurations (and files) in both the working and certified 
directories. If they’re the same it boots from the working directory, if they differ, it boots from the certified 
directory. 
Let’s reboot the switch, without telling it to specifically boot from the working directory: 
 
-> reload 
Confirm Reload (Y/N) : y 
 
When the switch reboots, check for the VLANs 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show vlan 
                              stree                 mble   src 
 vlan  type  admin   oper   1x1   flat   auth   ip   tag   lrn   name 
-----+-----+------+------+------+------+----+-----+-----+------+---------- 
   1    std   on    off     on    on     off    on   off     on   VLAN 1 
 
Notice they are gone, along with our session prompt and session timeout. This is because the switch booted 
from the certified directory.  
Enter the command to show what directory the switch booted from: 
-> show running-directory

2.1. 
User-defined Directory 
In Release 8, an OmniSwitch provides the ability to use also any user-defined directory in place of the WORKING 
one. Thus, allowing to have as much configuration file or AOS version as you need. 
The User-Defined Directory feature allows  
- to save and boot from user-defined directories. 
- To indicate the switch to use the configuration stored in this directory during a reboot. 
Type the following to create a user defined directory and copy the contents of the working directory to it: 
sw7 (6860-A) -> mkdir lab 
sw7 (6860-A) -> cp working/*.* lab 
cp: can't open 'working/boot.md5': Permission denied 
 
 
Tips 
The lab directory may have been already created, ignore error and proceed on. 
During the copy; it tries to copy the boot.md5 file but a “permission denied” message is displayed. This file is 
auto generated so ignore this error and proceed.

on which it had previously started with that stored in the directory CERTIFIED 
- If it was "WORKING" comparison between WORKING and CERTIFIED 
- IF it was on a user directory: comparison between User directory (e.g. lab) and CERTIFIED 
- If the configuration is different, the switch starts in the CERTIFIED directory

 1 
Configuration Snapshot / Text Based Configuration 
The configuration snapshot feature allows a text file to be created based on the current running configuration. 
This file can then be uploaded from the switch, manipulated, and applied to other switches. 
 
 
In this exercise, you can use the 6450-A to test the commands in R6 and the 6860-A to test the 
commands in R8   
 
- Remember that the command “more” enables the more, or page mode for your console screen display. 
This will display 24 lines per page by default. 
- Type the following: 
-> more 
-> show configuration snapshot all 
! Stack Manager : 
! Chassis : 
system name vxTarget 
system timezone +00:00 
system daylight savings time disable 
! Configuration: 
! VLAN : 
vlan 1 enable name "VLAN 1" 
vlan 2 enable name "VLAN 2" 
vlan 3 enable name "VLAN 3" 
vlan 99 enable name "VLAN 99" 
! VLAN SL: 
! IP : 
ip service all 
ip interface dhcp-client vlan 1 ifindex 1 
ip interface "Loopback0" address 10.3.3.3 
! IPMS : 
! AAA : 
aaa authentication console "local" 
! PARTM : 
! 802.1x : 
! QOS : 
! Policy manager : 
! Session manager : 
More? [next screen <sp>, next line <cr>, filter pattern </>, quit <q>]q 
- The above command list your current running configuration on the screen.  
- You can capture also your configuration to a text file. Type the following. 
-> configuration snapshot all snapall 
- The above command creates a snapshot of the entire switch configuration and copies it to a file called 
snapall in the current directory. Type the following: 
-> vi snapall (R6/R8) 
 
 
Entering ‘vi’ will allow you to use the vi editor to edit the file; to exit from viewing the 
snapshot file enter <esc> :q  
- The ‘more’ command can be used as an alternative to view the file.  
-> more snapall 
!========================================! 
! File: /flash/snapall                   ! 
!========================================!

! Chassis : 
system name vxTarget 
system timezone +00:00 
system daylight savings time disable 
! Configuration: 
! VLAN : 
vlan 1 enable name "VLAN 1" 
vlan 2 enable name "VLAN 2" 
vlan 3 enable name "VLAN 3"

It isn’t necessary to create a snapshot of the entire switch configuration. We should already have 3 VLANs 
created (2 3 and 99), if not create them. To create a snapshot of only the VLAN configuration enter the 
following: 
-> configuration snapshot vlan snapvlan 
- This will copy only the VLAN configuration to a file called snapvlan in the current directory. This can be 
applied and will only apply the changes in the file, leaving all other configuration intact.  Additional 
options can be specified for creating snapshots. 
- Enter the following to see the additional parameters and experiment with creating additional snapshots. 
-> configuration snapshot ? 
                          ^ 
                          WEBMGT VLAN UDLD TEST-OAM SYSTEM STP

                          AIP AAA 802.1Q 
 (AAA & Configuration Mgr Command Set) 
- A syntax check can be run on a configuration snapshot before it is applied to ensure there are no errors. 
Enter: 
-> configuration syntax check snapvlan verbose (R6) 
-> configuration syntax-check snapvlan verbose (R8)

Directories and CLI Structure 
 
 1 
Operating System 
The switch can be configured using SNMP (OmniVista), WebView or CLI. In this section, we’ll concentrate on 
CLI, its syntax, and its line-editing feature. CLI gives you the ability to search for parameters if the complete 
command is not known as well as recall and edit previous commands. 
1.1. 
Command Entry Rules and Syntax 
- 
When you start a session on the switch, you can execute CLI commands as soon as you are logged in. 
- 
The following rules apply: 
Enter only one command per line. 
Passwords are case sensitive. 
Commands are not case sensitive. The switch accepts commands entered in upper case, lower case or a 
combination of both. 
Press Enter to complete each command line entry. 
To use spaces within a user-defined text string, you must enclose the entry in quotation marks (“ ”). 
1.2. 
Using ‘?’ 
- 
A ‘?’ can be used to get a list of all possible commands, a list of commands that start with a letter or 
series of letters or a question mark can be entered after a command is started to get a list of available 
parameters.  
- 
Type the following: 
-> ? 
            ^ 
        COPY WRITE POWER TEMP-THRESHOLD TAKEOVER SYSTEM SHOW RRM RLS 
        RELOAD RDF RCP NO DEBUG CONFIGURE <cr> 
 (CMM Chassis Supervision Command Set) 
 
        WHOAMI WHO VIEW VI USER UPDATE UMOUNT TTY TFTP TELNET6 TELNET 
        SYSTEM SWLOG SSH6 SSH SHOW SFTP6 SFTP SESSION SCP-SFTP SCP RZ 
        RMDIR RM RESTORE RENAME PWD PROMPT NTP NSLOOKUP NO NEWFS MV MOVE 
        MOUNT MORE MODIFY MKDIR LS KILL IPV6 IP INSTALL HISTORY FTP6 FTP 
        FSCK FREESPACE EXIT DSHELL DIR DELETE DEBUG CP COMMAND-LOG CHMOD 
        CD BACKUP ATTRIB ALIAS 
 (System Service & File Mgmt Command Set) 
 
        SOURCE-LEARNING SHOW PORT-SECURITY NO MAC-ADDRESS-TABLE DEBUG  
 (Source Learning Command Set)................ 
 
-> v? 
            ^ 
        VIEW VI 
 (System Service & File Mgmt Command Set) 
 
        VLAN 
 (Vlan Command Set) 
 
-> vlan ? (R6) 
                ^ 
        PORT NO IPMVLAN 802.1Q <vid> <vlan1-vlan2> 
 (Vlan Command Set) 
 
-> vlan ? (R8) 
              ^ 
              <vlan> <vlan-vlan> 
 (Vlan Command Set)

<<<PAGE 234>>>
3 
Directories and CLI Structure 
 
- 
Notice the list of options available with the vlan command. Let's take it one step further: 
-> vlan port ? (R6) 
                     ^ 
                     MOBILE <slot/port_list> 
 (Vlan Command Set) 
 
-> vlan port  
- 
We could continue until we found the right parameters to accomplish what we were trying to do with 
the VLAN. 
- 
Experiment with this for some other commands such as ‘show ?’, ‘aaa ?’, or ‘copy ?’; this can be a 
useful feature when you are unsure of the entire command. 
- 
Also, entering a ‘?’ after a letter or string of letters, will list all commands that begin with that string as 
we saw above using 'v?'. 
1.3. 
Partial Keyword Completion  
- 
The CLI has a partial keyword recognition feature that allows the switch to recognize partial keywords to 
- 
CLI command syntax.  
- 
Instead of typing the entire keyword, you may type only as many characters as is necessary to uniquely 
identify the keyword, then press the Tab key.  
- 
The CLI will complete the keyword and place the cursor at the end of the keyword 
-> sh<tab> vl<tab>  
                              stree                 mble   src 
 vlan  type  admin   oper   1x1   flat   auth   ip   tag   lrn   name 
-----+-----+------+------+------+------+----+-----+-----+------+---------- 
   1    std   on    off     on    on     off    on   off     on   VLAN 1 
- 
You may use also auto-completion using the Space key on R6, by enabling the folloing command : 
-> session cli-auto-complete-space enable 
- 
Play with Tab and Space completion to understand the differences (essentially Space will not detect 
mistakes while Tab will do)  
1.4. 
Partial Keyword Abbreviation (R8) 
- 
The CLI has a partial keyword abbreviation feature that allows the switch to recognize partial keywords 
to CLI command syntax.  
- 
Instead of typing the entire keyword, you may type only as many characters as is necessary to uniquely 
identify the keyword. For example, ‘show vlan’ can be abbreviated to: 
-> sh vl 
 
 vlan    type   admin   oper    ip    mtu          name 
------+-------+-------+------+------+------+------------------ 
1      std       Ena     Dis   Dis    1500    VLAN 1 
4094   vcm       Ena     Dis   Dis    1500    VCM IPC 
- 
If the keyword cannot be uniquely identified an error will be displayed. The ‘?’ can be used to list the 
possible keywords. 
-> sh v 
 
ERROR: Invalid entry” “v” 
The letter ‘v’ does not uniquely identify a keyword and could stand for multiple keywords such as 
‘vlan’, 
‘violation’ or ‘verbose’.

Directories and CLI Structure 
 
 2 
CLI Line Editor and History 
Some additional capabilities of the CLI are to display the last command entered, modify commands, scroll 
through previous commands, and to re-enter a specific previously entered command. By default a feature called 
Command History is enabled. Command History retains the last 30 command issued DURING THE CURRENT 
LOGIN SESSION (not to be confused with Command Logging discussed later). 
- 
To re-play the previous command type the following: 
-> !! 
-> show vlan 
 
 
Tips 
On R8, the command is executed after!!.  
On R6, you need to confirm the command by pressing enter, so you can modify it. 
To recall the last command executed by the switch, press either the Up Arrow key or the !! (bang, bang) 
command at the prompt and the previous command will display on your screen. 
 
- 
You can also display a list of previously entered commands, copy one of those commands to the CLI, 
modify it if needed, and re-enter it. Type the following: 
 
-> show history (R6) 
-> history (R8) 
1 write memory 
2 show running-directory 
3 ls /flash/working 
4 show microcode working 
5 show microcode certified 
6 ls /flash/working 
7 ls /flash/certified 
8 dir 
9 dir /working 
10 reload working no rollback-timeout 
11 show running-directory 
12 reload 
13 show microcode 
14 ? 
15 v? 
16 vlan ? 
17 vlan port ? 
18 vlan port mobile ? 
19 vlan port mobile 
20 po? 
21 vl? 
22 show vlan 
23 show history 
 
-> !# (‘#’ = command number) 
- 
Now we could recall a line number and edit it as necessary using left/right arrow keys and/or backspace: 
-> !22 
-> show vlan 
- 
You can also bring up the last command that begins with a specific string or prefix. Bring up the last 
command previously entered that begins with ‘show’.  
- 
Enter: 
-> !show 
-> show history

 3 
Directory Structure/Commands 
3.1. 
Directory Structure 
- 
It is important to understand the directory structure of an OmniSwitch.  Different directories store 
different configurations on the switch.  
- 
In release 6, there are two main directories, flash/working and flash/certified. Each contains an AOS 
and possibly a configuration for the switch.  
- 
The certified directory contains files that have been certified by an authorized user as the default files 
for the switch. Configuration changes CAN NOT be saved directly to the certified directory. 
- 
The working directory contains files that may or may not be altered from the certified directory. The 
working directory is a holding place for new files. Files in the working directory must be tested before 
committing them to the certified directory. You can save configuration changes to the working 
directory. 
- 
In release 8, User-defined directories are any other directories created by the user. These directories 
are similar to the working directory in that they can contain image and configuration files. These 
directories can have any name and can be used to store additional switch configurations. Configuration 
changes CAN be saved directly to any user-defined directory. 
3.2. 
Directory commands 
- 
The directory commands are applied to the switch file system and to files contained within the file 
system. When you first enter the flash directory, your login is located at the top of the directory tree. 
- 
The switch uses basic UNIX commands to create, delete, move and copy files and directories including:  
pwd – shows current directory. 
cd – changes directory. 
mkdir – creates a new directory. 
ls – lists contents of a directory. 
dir – lists contents of a directory. 
mv – moves a file.  
cp – copies a file. 
rm – removes a file.  
- 
To determine the Location in the File Structure 
-> pwd 
/flash 
- 
To display directory content 
-> ls

Secure Switch Access 
This lab is designed to familiarize you with the switch security features of an OmniSwitch. With this feature, 
users with different access rights and configuration abilities can be created.  
Security is an important element on an OmniSwitch. In this lab, we’ll discover how to create users and 
manipulate the read and write privileges on the switch.  
2.1. 
Remove existing users 
- Before you begin this lab, ensure there are no previous users created by removing the userDB file from the 
switch and reboot it. 
 
 
Tips 
On R8 Omniswitches, the userDB file is named userTable7 and is located on the system directory 
On R6 Omniswitches, the userDB file is named userTable5 and is located on the network directory 
 
- Type the following : 
R8 -> rm system/userTable7 
R8 -> reload from working no rollback-timeout 
 
R6 -> rm network/userTable6 
R6 -> reload working no rollback-timeout 
- After the reboot, view the list of users created by default by entering the following: 
-> show user

- You should see at least 2 users: admin and default.  Notice the read and write privileges for each user and 
domain, as well as the SNMP privileges. As you can see the default profile has no rights at all. 
- Admin – Default user with full capability to configure the switch and create additional users. 
- Default – This account cannot be used to login to the switch. These privileges are applied to all new 
users created on the switch. By default, new users have no privileges; however the privileges of the 
default user can be modified if desired.

Authenticated Switch Access 
Authenticated Switch Access (ASA) provides the ability to restrict which users are able to configure the 
switch remotely. Switch login attempts can be challenged via the local database, or a remote database such 
as RADIUS or LDAP. ASA applies to Telnet, FTP, SNMP, SSH, HTTP, and the console and modem ports. 
- Log back in as admin and enter the following to configure the switch to check the local database when a 
SSH connection is attempted.

Stacking management

<<<PAGE 255>>>
Stacking Roles
In a stack, a switch can handle 4 different roles:
Primary
It is the primary CMM role that support all the switch features (Management, Firmware upgrade, 
SNMP,  switch diagnostic, rollback…) and acts as the “Main” Controller switch in the Stack
Secondary
It is the backup CMM of the stack and is ready to handle the Primary role when the Primary 
switch takes over or fails
Idle
It is seen as a NI in a switch (Network Interface)
This switch is ready to handle the “Secondary” role in case of loss of Primary switch
Pass-Through
In case of Slot-ID duplication, the second stared switch gets “Pass-through” role
It is not part of the stack, but does not block the traffic going through it (no disruption of the 
stack)
Its “Slot-ID” has to be redefined, and restarted to become “Idle”
Stack Manager is the first process (present on all CMM’s) to be started for CMM 
role election during stack boot up

<<<PAGE 256>>>
Slot-ID Setup
A switch uses a unique Slot-ID in the stack
This Slot-ID can be
Dynamically assigned in case no “boot.slot.cfg” file (or in case of out-of-the-box)
All switches are interconnected and boot up within a 15s timer (MAC @ method)
The switch with the lowest MAC @ will get Slot-ID 1, and then gets the role Primary
The switch connected to the Primary switch on Stack port A, gets Slot-ID 2 and becomes Secondary
The switch connected on Stack port A of the secondary gets Slot-ID 3 and becomes Idle, and…
All switches are interconnected, but a timer of 15s elapses between each switch startup (switch 
uptime method)
The first started switch gets Slot-ID 1 and uses Primary role
The second started switch (but connected to the Primary), gets Slot-ID 2, and becomes Secondary
The third started switch, connected to one of the previous ones, gets Slot-ID 3, and becomes Idle…
Manually assigned, the Slot-ID is managed switch by switch 
All switches boot up simultaneously, the Slot-ID 1 become Primary…

Stacking R6 
 
 1 
Basic Stacking Operations 
In addition to their working as individual stand-alone switches, OmniSwitch 6450 switches can also be linked 
together to work as a single virtual chassis known as a stack. With stacks, users can easily expand their 
switching capacity simply by adding additional switches to the stack. In addition, stacks provide enhanced 
resiliency and redundancy features. 
 
- The terms module, switch, slot, and element are used to refer to individual switches within a stacked 
configuration. The terms Chassis Management Module (CMM) and management module refer to those 
switches operating in a stack either in the primary or secondary management roles. OmniSwitch 6450 
switches operating in an idle role are essentially acting as network interface modules and therefore may 
be referred to as Network Interfaces (NIs). 
 
 
Notes 
You cannot mix OS6450, OS6850 and OS6250 switches in the same stack - all switches in a stack must be from 
the same family but can be different models within the family. 
 
 
 
1.1. 
Primary Management Module Selection 
- For a stack of switches to operate as a virtual chassis, there must be a mechanism for dynamically 
selecting the switch within the stack that will assume the primary management role. There are three 
different methods for selecting the primary switch. These methods are: 
- 
Chassis Uptime 
- 
Saved slot number 
- 
Chassis MAC Address 
1.2. 
Using Saved Slot Information 
- The saved slot number is the slot number the switch will assume following a reboot. This information is 
stored in a switch’s boot.slot.cfg file; the switch reads its slot number assignment from this file while 
booting and assumes the specified slot number within the stack. 
- If switches in a stacked configuration have no preconfigured slot assignments, the slot number for each 
switch is dynamically assigned by the system software. Slot numbers can also be manually assigned by the 
user which is the recommended method for stacking.  
- On 6450-A, active the stacking link, define the slot number 1, activate the stacking mode and reload the 
switch: 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> interfaces 1/11-12 admin up 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> write memory 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> stack set slot 1 saved-slot 1 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> stack set slot 1 mode stackable reload 
- Do the same on 6450-B, but with slot number 2 : 
sw6 (OS6450-B) -> interfaces 1/11-12 admin up

1.3. 
Using the Chassis MAC Address 
- By default, the primary management role will be given to the switch with the lowest chassis MAC address. 
However, for this to occur, all switches in the stack must be booted within 15 seconds of each other. In 
addition, switches in the stack must have no preconfigured slot information (/flash/boot.slot.cfg). 
Because of these two conditions, the MAC address method for selecting the primary module usually occurs 
with new “out of the box” switches, or switches from which any preconfigured slot information has been 
cleared. 
1.4. 
Using Saved Slot Information 
- The saved slot number is the slot number the switch will assume following a reboot. This information is 
stored in a switch’s boot.slot.cfg file; the switch reads its slot number assignment from this file at bootup 
and assumes the specified slot number within the stack. 
- If switches in a stacked configuration have no preconfigured slot assignments, the slot number for each 
switch is dynamically assigned by the system software. Slot numbers can also be manually assigned by the 
user which is the recommended method for stacking.  
1.5. 
Using Switch uptime 
- A user can override both the MAC address and saved slot methods for determining a stack’s primary 
management module. This is done by controlling the uptime of switches in the stack. If all elements of a 
stack are powered off, the user can force a particular switch to become primary by powering on that 
switch and waiting a minimum of 15 seconds before powering on any other switches. This can be useful if 
the user wants a switch placed in a specific location, e.g., the top-most switch in a stack, to become the 
primary.  
- As with the lowest MAC address method, the primary management module is dynamically assigned slot 
number 1 when the stack is booted. 
 
 
Notes 
Although, for ease-of-management purposes, it is recommended that slot numbers are assigned beginning with 
slot number 1, it is not a requirement. In other words, a stack of four switches can have slot assignments 3, 4, 
5, and 6. However, it is important that each element in a stack is assigned a unique slot number. Do not assign 
duplicate slot numbers to elements in a stack. Otherwise, one or more switches will be forced into pass-
through mode. It is also recommended that Slot's are configured from the top down to ease of management 
purposes.

1.7. 
Recovering from Pass-Through Mode 
- The pass-through mode is a state in which a switch has attempted to join a stack but has been denied 
primary, secondary, or idle status. When a switch is in the pass-through mode, its Ethernet ports are 
brought down (i.e, they cannot pass traffic), however its stacking cable connections remain fully 
functional and can pass traffic through to other switches in the stack. In this way, the pass-through mode 
provides a mechanism to prevent the stack ring from being broken.  
- The most common reason for one or more switches to enter pass-through is duplicate slot number 
assignments within the stack. So, in order to avoid pass-through mode, it is useful to keep track of the 
current saved slot numbers on all elements in the stack. Slot number assignments are stored in the 
boot.slot.cfg file in the /flash directory of each switch. 
- If the stack is booted and the same slot number is discovered on two or more switches, the switch with 
the lowest MAC address is allowed to come up and operate normally. Meanwhile, switches with the 
duplicate slot number and a higher MAC address come up in pass-through mode. 
- Let's change our configuration a little bit, change the slot number of the switch that is currently slot 2 to 
be configured as slot 1 also. From the Primary switch: 
 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> stack set slot 2 saved-slot 1 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> reload  ni 2

Master/Slave Election
VFLs become operational -> Virtual Chassis protocol is started
3 basic functions:
Topology discovery (IS-IS)
Master Election
Keep-Alive / Hello messages for monitoring
Election of the Master chassis 
Based on (from higher to lower priority):
1)
Current Master Chassis 
2)
Higher chassis priority value

VIRTUAL CHASSIS REDUNDANCY & UPGRADE

<<<PAGE 305>>>
Virtual Chassis Redundancy
If the Master chassis goes down
The Slave chassis takes over the Master role
All traffic flows reconverge to the new Master
If the Slave chassis goes down
The Master chassis remains Master
All traffic flow reconverge to the existing Master
If a VFL goes down, but the chassis are still operational
The Master chassis retains its role
The Slave chassis transitions to assume the Master role as well 
Splitted topology, 2 Masters! 
Solution =====>
Note: having 2 Masters can results in problems, because the 2 switches are using the same IP and MAC address in the 
network
VFL
Master Chassis

<<<PAGE 306>>>
Split Chassis Detection
Remote Chassis Detection (RCD)
Each chassis sends periodic updates via the EMP port
If VFL fails, 
A Slave Chassis becomes Master (2 Master chassis)
Communication between the 2 switches is still possible through the EMP port
The former Slave chassis notices that the Master chassis is still up and running
To avoid any problem, the former Slave chassis disables its user ports
Limitation: EMP port mandatory to use this feature 
For example, an OmniSwitch 6860 doesn’t have such port!

Split Chassis Detection
Virtual Chassis Split Detection (VCSP)
EMP Ports not mandatory
Each VC chassis shares a link aggregate with the VCSP Helper
VCSP PDUs are sent from the Master via the VCSP Link Aggregate
If VFL fails, 
A Slave Chassis becomes Master (2 Masters chassis)
Communication between the 2 switches is still possible through the VCSP Link Aggregate
The former Slave chassis notices that the Master chassis is still up and running
To avoid any problem, the former Slave chassis disables its user ports

In Service Software Upgrade (ISSU)
Used to upgrade the software on a VC with minimal network disruption
Each element is upgraded individually
Step by Step
Upload new code, vcsetup.cfg and vcboot.cfg in a new directory (ex. issu_dir)
Launch the dedicated issu command 
The image and configuration files are then copied to all of the Slaves
The Slaves are then reloaded from the ISSU directory in order from lowest to highest chassis ID

Port Mirroring

<<<PAGE 337>>>
Overview
Port Mirroring
Copies all incoming and outgoing traffic from one switch port to another
Provides the ability to perform a packet capture
Ports supported
Ethernet, Fast/ Gigabit Ethernet, 10/ 40 Gigabit Ethernet
Sessions supported
2 per standalone switch and per stack
N-to-1 Mirroring Supported
128 to 1 all models
Port requirements - must be of identical capacity
R6/R8 -> port mirroring <id> source <s/s/p> destination <s/s/p>
R6 -> port mirroring 1 source 1/2-6 destination 2/4
R6 -> port mirroring 1 source 1/9 2/7 3/5 destination 2/4
R6 -> port mirroring 1 source 1/2-6 1/9 2/7 3/5 destination 2/4
R8 -> port-mirroring 1 source 1/1/2-6 1/1/9 1/2/7 1/3/5 destination 1/2/4

<<<PAGE 338>>>
Remote Port Mirroring (RPM) 
Allows traffic to be carried over the network to a remote switch
Achieved by using a dedicated remote port mirroring VLAN 
RPM VLAN has to be configured on the source, destination and intermediate 
switches 
No other traffic is allowed on that VLAN
The following types of traffic will not be mirrored:
Link Aggregation Control Packets (LACP), 802.1AB (LLDP), 802.1x port authentication,  
802.3ag (OAM), Layer 3 control packets, Generic Attribute Registration Protocol 
(GARP)
SOURCE PORT
DESTINATION PORT
INTERMEDIATE SWITCH
SOURCE SWITCH
DESTINATION SWITCH

<<<PAGE 339>>>
Policy Based Mirroring
Mirroring is done based on a QoS policy instead of a specific port
1 session supported at any given time
Port Based Mirroring. It can be done on incoming or outgoing traffic or both.
policy action mirror
Mirror traffic based on
Source & Destination addresses
Address pairs
Protocols
VLAN classification
Port mirroring and monitoring cannot be configured on the same NI
MIRRORING POLICY
INGRESS, EGRESS, OR BOTH INGRESS & EGRESS PACKETS
POLICY ACTION & PORT ASSIGNMENT
DIRECT TRAFFIC TO MIRROR PORT

<<<PAGE 340>>>
Policy Based Mirroring
Example 1
-> policy condition c1 source ip 1.1.1.1
-> policy action a1 ingress egress mirror 1/1
-> policy rule r1 condition c1 action a1
-> qos apply
Policy rule r1 will cause all packets with a source IP of 1.1.1.1 to be ingress and egress 
mirrored to port 1/1
Example 2
-> policy condition c1 source ip 1.1.1.1
-> policy action a2 ingress egress mirror 1/1 disposition drop
-> policy rule r2 condition c1 action a2
-> qos apply
Policy rule r2 drops traffic with a source IP of 1.1.1.1, but the mirrored traffic from 
this source is not dropped and is forwarded to port 1/1

Port monitoring

<<<PAGE 342>>>
Port Monitoring
Captures data and stores in Sniffer format on switch
Ports supported
Ethernet, Fast/ Gigabit Ethernet, 10/40 Gigabit Ethernet
Captures first 64-bytes of frame
Session supported per switch or stack: 1
Default file size:
R6: 16 KB (max = 160 KB)
R7/R8: 64 KB (max = 2 MB)
Round-Robin or stop capture when max storage reached
Cannot use port monitoring and mirroring on same port
Data stored in compliance with the ENC file format (Network General Sniffer 
Format)
R6/R8 -> port monitoring 6 source 1/2/3 enable
6 – session ID
Session can be paused, resumed, disabled and associated with a timeout
-> show port monitor file

<<<PAGE 343>>>
Remote monitoring

<<<PAGE 344>>>
Remote Monitoring - RMON
RMON probes are used to collect, interpret and forward statistical data about 
network traffic from designated active ports in a LAN segment
Can be monitored using OmniVista
4 groups supported:
Ethernet Statistics – Gather Ethernet port statistics (e.g. port utilization, error statistics)
History Group - Stores sampling such as utilization and error count
Alarms Group – Compare samplings to thresholds (e.g. absolute or relative, rising and falling 
thresholds)
Events Group – Controls generation an notification to NMS station

-> rmon probes stats enable

2 
Switch maintenance and Diagnostics tools 
 
 1 
Switch Logging 
Switch Logging can be used to track informational or debugging messages from the switch. This is 
dependent upon the severity level set for a particular process. Logging can be configured to send its output 
to flash, console, or an external server.  By default switch logging is enabled. 
- On the 6860-A, type the following : 
6860-A -> show swlog 
Operational Status                 : Running, 
File Size per file                 : 1250 Kbytes, 
Log Device 1                       : console flash, 
Syslog FacilityID                  : local0(16), 
Hash Table entries age limit       : 60 seconds, 
Switch Log Preamble                : Enabled, 
Switch Log Debug                   : Disabled, 
Switch Log Duplicate Detection     : Enabled, 
Console Display Level              : info 
- You should see that logging is running and sending its output to both flash and the console. It does not 
mean that all messages will be displayed on the console, only messages matching the severity level, by 
default, informational (6). Logging can be disabled if desired.  
- Type the following: 
6860-A -> swlog disable 
 
6860-A -> show swlog 
Operational Status                 : Not Running, 
File Size per file                 : 1250 Kbytes, 
Log Device 1                       : console flash, 
Syslog FacilityID                  : local0(16), 
Hash Table entries age limit       : 60 seconds, 
Switch Log Preamble                : Enabled, 
Switch Log Debug                   : Disabled, 
Switch Log Duplicate Detection     : Enabled, 
Console Display Level              : info 
- To re-enable logging enter : 
6860-A -> swlog enable 
- The logging feature has a number of application IDs. These IDs are used to determine which process 
generated the logging message and at what severity level. Consult the user guide for a list of processes 
and associated severity levels. By default all processes are set to a severity level of 6, which is 
informational, as indicated above. All logging messages are stored in the swlog*.log files and can be 
viewed right on the switch. 
6860-A -> show log swlog 
 
 
Notes 
Use CTRL+C keys to stop the display of the file. 
You may also use show log swlog | grep “string to find” or show log swlog timestamp mm/dd/yy 
hh:mm:ss to find specific information on the log file.

<<<PAGE 353>>>
3 
Switch maintenance and Diagnostics tools 
 
 2 
Command Logging 
Like switch logging, commands entered on the OmniSwitch can captured to a log file. These can then be 
reviewed at a later time to see what changes have been made. This is a very valuable tool, especially when 
doing changes to your configurations.  
- Type the following : 
6860-A -> show command-log 
 
6860-A -> command-log enable 
- Let's create and delete a couple of VLAN's to demonstrate: 
6860-A -> vlan 4-5 
 
6860-A -> no vlan 4-5 
 
6860-A -> show command-log 
Command : no vlan 4-5 
  UserName : admin 
  Date     : Tue Feb 11 03:54:58 
  Ip Addr  : console 
  Result   : SUCCESS 
 
Command : vlan 4-5 
  UserName : admin 
  Date     : Tue Feb 11 03:54:53 
  Ip Addr  : console 
  Result   : SUCCESS 
 
Command : command-log enable 
  UserName : admin 
  Date     : Tue Feb 11 03:53:33 
  Ip Addr  : console 
  Result   : SUCCESS 
 
- You should now see the commands you entered displayed on the screen with information about the time 
and where they were entered from, such as a console or TELNET session. 
- To disable it enter : 
6860-A -> command-log disable

Switch maintenance and Diagnostics tools 
 
 3 
Port Mirroring 
Port mirroring can be configured to copy traffic from one or multiple ports to another. The destination port 
would normally have a traffic analyzer connected.   
- Let’s create a mirroring session to copy traffic from one port to another.  
6860-A -> port-mirroring 1 source port 1/1/1 destination port 1/1/10 
 
6860-A -> port-mirroring 1 enable 
 
6860-A -> show port-mirroring status 1 
 
 Session    Mirror        Mirror      Unblocked   RPMIR     Config    Oper 
           Destination    Direction     Vlan       Vlan     Status    Status 
----------+-----------+--------------+----------+---------+----------+--------- 
   1.        1/1/10           -         NONE      NONE       Enable    On 
----------+-----------+--------------+----------+---------+----------+--------- 
           Mirror 
           Source 
----------+-----------+--------------+----------+---------+----------+--------- 
   1.         1/1/1      bidirectional     -         -         Enable    On 
 
 
- To remove a port mirroring session, enter : 
 
6860-A -> no port-mirroring 1 
 
 
The maximum number of mirroring sessions is limited to two. 
 4 
Port Monitoring 
Port Monitoring makes it possible to capture traffic being sent to and from a port and store it in  /flash in 
".enc" (or Sniffer) format. The data is stored in a file named pmon.enc by default, but this can be modified. 
The file can then be transferred off the switch and viewed in detail using a traffic analyzer. It is also 
possible to display the output directly to the console or to a telnet session.  
- Start a port monitoring session : 
6860-A -> port-monitoring 1 source port 1/1/1 enable 
 
6860-A -> show port-monitoring status 
 
 Sess Mon.    Mon. Over  Oper.  Admin  Capt.   Max.   File 
      Src     Dir  write Stat   Stat   Type    Size   Name 
-----+-------+----+-----+------+------+-------+------+----------------------- 
  1.   1/1/1  Bi    ON     ON    ON   Brief     64K  /flash/pmonitor.enc 
- Generate traffic from client by issuing pings to any reachable address. 
- The session can be paused and resumed if necessary, type the following: 
6860-A -> port-monitoring 1 pause 
 
6860-A -> show port-monitoring status 
 
 Sess Mon.    Mon. Over  Oper.  Admin  Capt.   Max.   File 
      Src     Dir  write Stat   Stat   Type    Size   Name 
-----+-------+----+-----+------+------+-------+------+----------------------- 
  1.   1/1/1  Bi    ON    OFF     ON   Brief    64K   /flash/pmonitor.enc 
 
6860-A -> port-monitoring 1 resume 
 
6860-A -> port-monitoring 1 disable 
WARNING: 
Monitored data is available in file /flash/pmonitor.enc

Dynamic VLAN Membership

<<<PAGE 366>>>
Dynamic VLAN Membership
Dynamic VLANs
VLAN is assigned depending on the device or the user
Device oriented : VLAN according to traffic criteria (MAC@, etc…)
User oriented: Authenticated VLAN (IEEE 802.1x  for enhanced security)

<<<PAGE 367>>>
Dynamic VLAN Membership 
Dynamic Assignment
Applies only to mobile (R6) or UNP (R8)* ports
Requires additional configuration of VLAN rules or UNP classification rules* 
When traffic is received on a mobile port: 
The packets are examined to determine if their content matches any of the VLAN 
rules configured on the switch 
If so, the mobile port is assigned to that VLAN
Rules are defined by specifying a port, MAC address, protocol, network 
address, binding, or DHCP criteria 
It is also possible to define multiple rules for the same VLAN 
*UNP ports and classification rules are covered in a different module

<<<PAGE 368>>>
Precedence/Rule Type
Upon receiving a frame, Source Learning compares the frame with VLAN 
Policies in Order
For more information about the precedence/rule type, please refer to the 
technical documentation
1. MAC Address
2. MAC Range
3. Network Address 
4. Protocol
5. Default (No Match -> port default VLAN)

<<<PAGE 369>>>
VLAN Mobility
Default VLAN Management
Default VLAN
-> vlan port slot/port default vlan {enable | disable}
Enabled -> user will join default VLAN when no rule matches (default)
Disabled -> user’s traffic will be dropped, when no rule matches
Default VLAN restore
-> vlan port slot/port default vlan restore {enable | disable}
Enabled -> user will join default VLAN when traffic ages out (default)
Disabled -> user will remain in the VLAN membership even after traffic ages out

VLAN Creation 
VLANs provide the ability to segregate a network into multiple broadcast domains. Additionally, Virtual Router 
ports can be assigned to VLANs to allow traffic to be switched at Layer 3. 
- In its default configuration, the switch has only one VLAN; VLAN 1. This is the default VLAN and all ports 
are initially associated with it. This VLAN CANNOT be deleted, but it can be disabled if so desired. 
- Let’s run the command to see the VLANs that exist on the switch as well as information on a single VLAN. 
- On 6450-A (switch 5), type the following:  
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show vlan 
                              stree                 mble   src 
 vlan  type  admin   oper   1x1   flat   auth   ip   tag   lrn   name 
-----+-----+------+------+------+------+----+-----+-----+------+---------- 
   1    std   on    off     on    on     off   off   off     on   VLAN 1 
4001    std   on     on     on    on     off    on   off     on   Administration 
 
- Reference the User Guides for details on each column: 
vlan –  The VLAN ID number 
type - The type of VLAN (std, vstk, gvrp or ipmv) 
admin – Administrative status 
oper – Operational Status (Any active ports associated with the VLAN) 
1X1 – 1X1 Spanning Tree Status – (on/off) 
flat – Flat Spanning Tree Status – (Is 802.1s Enabled) 
auth –  Authenticated VLAN status 
ip – IP status (Has an IP address been associated with the VLAN) 
ipx – IPX status (Has an IPX address been associated with the VLAN) 
mble tag – mobility tag (on/off) 
src lrn – Source Learning status (on/off) 
name – VLAN name 
- To display information on a specific VLAN: 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show vlan 1 
Name                : VLAN 1, 
Administrative State: enabled, 
Operational State   : disabled, 
1x1 Spanning Tree State : enabled, 
Flat Spanning Tree State : enabled, 
IP Router Port      : off, 
Mobile Tag          : off, 
Source Learning     : enabled

- In order to have IP connectivity to a VLAN interface (not required for connectivity to other clients/servers 
within a VLAN), an IP address must be assigned to a Virtual Router port and associated to that VLAN. This 
IP address can then be used for IP connectivity as well as Layer 3 switching. In order to do this, we first 
create the IP address and then associate it to a VLAN.   
- Type the following (int_1 is the VLAN alias, 192.168.10.5 is the IP interface address) 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> ip interface int_1 address 192.168.10.5/24 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show ip interface

admin                            10.4.17.5       255.255.255.0       UP     YES vlan 4001 
int_1                            192.168.10.5    255.255.255.0     DOWN      NO unbound 
- Notice we did not associate a VLAN with the interface yet, this is indicated by the 'unbound' status in the 
Device column. To bind a VLAN: 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> ip interface int_1 vlan 1

-> ip interface int_1 address 192.168.10.5/24 vlan 1

VLANS 
 
- Take note of the Status field. If it reads DOWN, this indicates no active ports or devices have been 
associated with the VLAN that the Virtual Router has been assigned to. If a Virtual Router interface is 
down, it cannot be connected to, will not reply to PING requests nor will it be advertised in any router 
updates. This will not affect the Layer 2 broadcast domain, however. 
- Let’s activate a port in VLAN 1 to change the status to UP. 
- The client 5 VM is already connected to port 1/1 of switch 5, but interface is down, to activate it, type : 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> interfaces 1/1 admin up 
 
 
Notes 
In release 8, command is  
 
 
-> interface 1/1/1 admin-state enable 
 
- Then check the port status 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show vlan 1 port 
  port     type      status 
--------+---------+-------------- 
  1/1     default   forwarding 
  1/2     default     inactive 
  1/3     default     inactive 
  1/4     default     inactive 
- Since all ports currently belong to VLAN 1, this will now cause VLAN 1 to become active.  Run the 
command to check the status of the IP interface to see this. 
- Type the following : 
sw5 (OS6450-A) -> show ip interface 
Total 3 interfaces 
             Name                   IP Address     Subnet Mask   Status Forward  Device

int_1                            192.168.10.5    255.255.255.0       UP     YES vlan 1 
- Now that the VLAN has an active port, let’s modify the IP information of PC1 and PING the router 
interface associated with VLAN 1. Perform the following: 
- Open a console to Client 5 from vSphere 
- Go to the Network Connections window and right-click on ‘Pod’ connection. Select Properties.

should now have IP connectivity.

Additional VLANs creation 
Currently there is only the default VLAN created on the switch (except for the administration one). The 
following steps will provide information on creating another VLAN, enabling IP on the VLAN, moving ports 
into the VLAN, and forwarding IP packets between VLANs. 
- To begin, let’s create a new VLAN and assign an IP address to that VLAN as done previously;

Overview
What is Link Aggregation?
Method of aggregating (combining) more than 2 ports/links so that the switch will 
“see” them as one logical link
Advantages of Link Aggregation?
Scalability
Reliability
Ease of Migration
Provides an aggregated link
(multiple physical links combined into one logical link)
Logical Link can be statically assigned to any VLAN
802.1q can be configured on the logical aggregated link

<<<PAGE 395>>>
Specifications
Static (OmniChannel) or Dynamic (IEEE 802.3ad/LACP) 
Maximum of 256 link aggregation ports per switch
Number of links per group supported: 2, 4, 8 or16
10-Mbps, 100-Mbps, 1-Gbps, or 10-Gbps Ethernet links
2 ports per group - maximum 128 link aggregate groups
4 ports per group – maximum 64 link aggregate groups
8 ports per group – maximum 32 link aggregate groups 
16 ports per group – maximum 16 link aggregate groups 
One port can only belong to one link aggregation

<<<PAGE 396>>>
Static vs. Dynamic
Difference between Static and Dynamic
Static
Port parameters MUST be exactly the same at both ends and within the group
same speed (e.g., all 10 Mbps, all 100 Mbps, all 1 Gigabit, or all 10 Gigabit)
Only works between Alcatel-Lucent OmniSwitches
Dynamic
IEEE 802.3ad LACP
LACP will negotiate the optimal parameters for both ends using LACPDU (Link Aggregation 
Control Protocol Data Unit)
Ports must be of the same speed within the same aggregate group 
It also works between two different devices such as switches, servers and 
storage systems.

<<<PAGE 397>>>
Static Link Aggregation Groups - CLI
Creating a Static Aggregate Group 
-> static linkagg <agg_num> size <size> admin state enable (R6)
-> linkagg static agg <agg_num> size <size> admin-state enable (R8)
Adding Ports to a Static Aggregate Group
-> static agg <slot/port> agg <agg_num> (R6)
-> linkagg static port <slot/port>* agg <agg_num> (R8)
Removing Ports from a Static Aggregate Group
-> static agg no <slot/port> (R6)
-> no linkagg static port <slot/port>* (R8)

<<<PAGE 398>>>
Dynamic Link Aggregation Groups - CLI
Configuring a Dynamic Link Aggregation Group
-> lacp linkagg <agg_num> size <size> admin state enable (R6)
-> lacp linkagg <agg_num> actor admin key <actor_admin_key> (R6)
-> linkagg lacp agg <agg_num> size <size> admin-state enable (R8)
-> linkagg lacp agg <agg_num>
actor admin-key <actor_admin_key> (R8)
Assigning ports to the Dynamic Link Aggregation Group
-> lacp agg <slot/port> actor admin key <actor_admin_key> (R6)   
-> linkagg lacp agg <slot/port>* actor admin-key <actor_admin_key> (R8)
Actor admin key must be configured to the same value on both ends of the link 
aggregation group
*chassis/slot/port for R8

Load Balancing Multicast on Link Aggregation Groups
Multicast traffic is by default forwarded through the primary port of the Link 
Aggregation Group
User has the option to enable hashing for non-unicast traffic, which will load 
balance the non-unicast traffic across all ports in the Link Aggregation Group
If non-ucast option is not specified, link aggregation will only load balance unicast
packets
-> hash-control {brief | extended [udp-tcp-port] | load-balance non-
ucast {enable | disable}}

Link Aggregation 
 
 1 
Topology 
Link Aggregation provides the ability to combine multiple physical ports into a single logical port for added 
throughput and redundancy; this can be done statically using OmniChannel or dynamically using the IEEE 
802.3ad (LACP) protocol. 
 
 
 
 2 
Link Aggregation – Dynamic 
2.1. 
Create a Dynamic Link Aggregation 
- Now, we will define a dynamic link aggregate, assign the group ID 5 as we did previously and size it at 2 
ports.   
- Type: 
6450 -> lacp linkagg 5 size 2 actor admin key 5  
6860 -> linkagg lacp agg 5 size 2 actor admin-key 5  
- Unlike static link aggregations where we physically assigned the ports to the link aggregation number, 
ports are associated to a dynamic link aggregation using the actor admin key. Although in the above 
example the actor admin key matches the link agg number, this is not a requirement as the admin key has 
local significance only.  
-> show linkagg 
                                   
Number  Aggregate  SNMP Id   Size  Admin State  Oper State     Att/Sel Ports 
-------+----------+---------+----+------------+--------------+------------- 
   5     Dynamic   40000005   2      ENABLED      DOWN            0   0 
 
- Notice we have no ports associated, using the actor admin key assigned to the link aggregation, let's 
associate the ports: 
6450 -> lacp agg 1/11 actor admin key 5 
6450 -> lacp agg 1/12 actor admin key 5 
 
6860 -> linkagg lacp port 1/1/23-24 actor admin-key 5

802.1q 
 
 1 
Topology 
In a Layer 2 environment the Ports default VLAN is used for bridging traffic across a physical connection 
between switches. In an IEEE 802.1Q environment, the Default VLAN for the port is bridged all other VLANs 
will have the IEEE 802.1Q tag inserted for proper VLAN association at the remote side. 
 
 2 
Bridged VLAN Physical Connections

2.2. 
Configure 802.1Q 
- Our VLAN 20 and 30 IP interfaces are currently down because we have no members in the two VLANs. 
Remember, if there are no members of a VLAN the IP interface is not only down but will not be advertised 
to the Layer 3.  
- Normally, to have Layer 2 connectivity between the two switches for all three VLANs, three physical links 
would be required. However, we will configure 802.1Q tagging to carry data from all three VLANs over 
physical link. 
- Type the following 
6450-A -> vlan 20 802.1q 5 
6450-A -> vlan 30 802.1q 5 
 
6450-B -> vlan 20 802.1q 5 
6450-B -> vlan 30 802.1q 5 
6450-B -> vlan 20 802.1q 1/3 
6450-B -> vlan 30 802.1q 1/3 
 
6860-A -> vlan 20 members linkagg 5 tagged 
6860-A -> vlan 30 members linkagg 5 tagged 
 
6860-B -> vlan 20 members linkagg 5 tagged 
6860-B -> vlan 30 members linkagg 5 tagged 
6860-B -> vlan 20 members port 1/1/3 tagged 
6860-B -> vlan 30 members port 1/1/3 tagged

- You should now be able to ping any address in our example network because each switch is tagging the 
data over the link between two switches; allowing each packet to be sent over the same physical link, 
while remaining in the correct VLAN as it is forwarded to the remote switch. How is your PC 
communicating? Are packets being bridged? Routed? Both? How do you know?

Reminder
Purpose
Prevent network loops
Automatic reconfiguration in case of a topology change
How it Works? 
Lowest Mac switch will be elected as ROOT Bridge (SW-A)
All the ports on the ROOT Bridge will be Designated Port (DP) and will be in 
forwarding status
Non ROOT Bridge will have ROOT Port (lowest port number of the Root Bridge)
Redundant link Port on the Non Root Bridge will be in Blocked status
STP runs by default on the OmniSwitches

<<<PAGE 419>>>
Spanning Tree Protocol (IEEE 802.1D)
Defined in IEEE 802.1D as a protocol that detects and prevents loops in a network
Between any 2 logical LANs
Only 1 Forwarding path
Rest of the paths in Blocking mode
STP provides recovery from bridge failures by changing blocked interfaces to a forwarding 
state, if a primary link fails 
How it works:
BPDUs are exchanged among the Switches/Bridges
Root bridge selection based on 
lowest numerical bridge priority (0 to 65535)
If same priority, use of lowest MAC address
Port roles
Root Port and Designated Ports
BPDU with the lowest value (Bridge ID, Path Cost and/or Port MAC) will decide the Root Port
Others will be designed as Designated or Disabled ports
A logical tree will then be built with the Root Bridge at the top of the tree (an inverted 
tree)
Physical changes of the network force spanning-tree recalculation







Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (IEEE 802.1w)
RSTP - Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol
Defined in IEEE 802.1w as a protocol to provide for subsecond reconvergence of STP 
after failure of one of the links
Faster convergence time
With IEEE 802.1w, instead of ports going into a Blocking mode, they are now in 
standby mode
Once the forwarding port fails (thru the detection of the data-link layer), the standby 
port will immediately take over
Interoperates with IEEE 802.1D
RSTP calculates final topology using exactly the same criteria as IEEE 802.1D

<<<PAGE 422>>>
RSTP Convergence Time
IEEE 802.1D states disabled, blocking, 
and listening have been merged into a 
unique 802.1w discarding state
3 port states
Faster convergence time

<<<PAGE 423>>>
Port Roles
Root Port
Provides the best path (lowest cost) to the root switch
Designated Port
Connects the LAN to the designated bridge. 
This bridge provides the LAN with the shortest path to the root
Alternate Port 
Offers an alternate path to the root bridge if the root port on its own bridge goes 
down
Backup Port 
Provides a backup connection for the designated port. It can only exist when there are 
redundant designated port connections to the LAN
Disabled Port 
Port is not operational

Flat Mode
Sw1 & 2 runs on flat mode, hence port 1/2-3 are in Blocking
One STP instance for the entire switch
Port states are determined across VLANs
Multiple connections between switches are considered redundant paths even if 
they are configured in different VLANs
STP parameters are configured for VLAN 1
Fixed (untagged) and 802.1Q tagged ports are supported in each VLAN
BPDU always untagged
When the Spanning Tree mode is changed from 1x1 to flat, ports still retain 
their VLAN associations but are now part of a single Spanning Tree instance 
that spans across all VLANs

1x1 Mode
Single STP instance enabled for each VLAN configured on the switch
Each STP instance have a spanning-tree topology independent of other 
spanning-tree instances
Provides multiple forwarding paths for data traffic
Enables load balancing
Maximum VLAN (or Spanning Tree) instances per switch:
R6 = 252
R7 = 128
R8 = 100

<<<PAGE 430>>>
1x1 Mode (aka Per VLAN Mode) 
Enabled by default
Port state undetermined on a per VLAN basis
Fixed (untagged) ports single STP instance -> configured Port default VLAN
802.1Q tagged ports participate in an 802.1Q STP instance allowing it to extend 
across tagged VLANs
If a VLAN contains both fixed and tagged ports
A hybrid of the 2 Spanning Tree instances (single and 802.1Q) is applied
If a VLAN appears as a tag on a port, then the BPDU for that VLAN are also tagged
If a VLAN appears as the configured default VLAN for the port, then BPDU are not 
tagged and the single Spanning Tree instance applies

<<<PAGE 437>>>
Overview
IEEE 802.1s standard 
Based on RSTP (same convergence time/ports’ states/ports’ roles) 
Introduces the concept of “Spanning Tree Instances”
Possibility to map several VLANs to one instance
One BPDU is exchanged for all instances over default VLAN
Multiple Spanning Tree Region concept

<<<PAGE 442>>>
Terminology
CST Root
The bridge with the lowest priority bridge id in the whole Network is selected as the CST 
Root 
Within the MST Region, the CST Root Path Cost remains constant.
CIST Regional Root 
One bridge in a region whose path cost to the CST Root is the lowest is selected as the CIST 
Regional Root
CIST Root Port
Provides the minimum cost path from a bridge to the CST root (if the bridge is not the CST 
root)
The Path is always through the CIST Regional root (if the bridge is not the regional root)
MSTI Regional Root 
One bridge in a region is independently selected for each MSTI to be the MSTI regional root
Designated Ports
Provides the least cost path from an attached LAN  to CST root through a bridge
Alternate and Backup Ports
Provides connectivity if any other bridges or ports fail

Ethernet Ring Protocol (ERP)

<<<PAGE 450>>>
Overview
ITU-T recommendation draft G.8032/Y.1344 specifies the protection switching 
mechanisms and protocol for Ethernet rings topologies
Ethernet Ring Protection (ERP) is a protection switching mechanism for Ring 
topologies like multi-ring/ladder network
Automatic Protection Switching (APS) protocol is used to coordinate the prevention 
of network loops within a bridged Ethernet Ring
ERP convergence time of 50ms can be achieved on a typical ring during a node or 
link failure
Loop prevention is achieved by allowing the traffic to flow on all but one of the 
links within the protected Ethernet ring
A ring operates in two mode

Idle – meaning normal operation; all links up and RPL is blocked

Protection – meaning protection switching activated; a ring failure has triggered the RPL 
into a forwarding state
ERP uses the special destination MAC address 01:19:A7:00:00:01 for the protocol 
PDUs

<<<PAGE 451>>>
Ring Ports
Each ring node is connected to two 
adjacent nodes using two independent 
links called Ring Link
The port for a Ring Link is called a Ring 
Port
Loop prevention is achieved by allowing 
the traffic to flow on all but one of the 
links within the protected Ethernet ring

This link is called the Ring Protection Link 
(RPL)

Under normal conditions this link is blocked
The node connected to an RPL within the 
ring is designated as the RPL owner

RPL Owner is responsible for blocking the  
traffic on the RPL under normal condition

RPL Owner is responsible for unblocking the 
RPL under a ring failure/node failure
Ring Port
RPL Owner
RPL Connection 
Point (Blocked)

<<<PAGE 452>>>
Link Failure
Ring Nodes/Links are monitored to detect the failure, Ring APS (R-APS) 
messages are sent to RPL owner to inform failed condition
Adjacent node sends out the R-APS message of Signal Failure (SF)
R-APS(SF) message triggers the RPL owner to unblock the RPL link
All nodes in the ring flush the dynamic MAC addresses learned on their ring ports 
The ring is now operating in protection mode
Ring Port
RPL Owner
RPL Connection 
Point (Unblocked)
Blocked Port
Unblocked Port

<<<PAGE 453>>>
Link Recovery
When the failed link or node recovers, the ring will transition back to idle 
mode
Adjacent node of the recovered link will initiate an R-APS message of No Request 
(NR) and start the Guard Timer (GT)
GT prevents the nodes from receiving outdated R-APS messages that are no longer relevant. Any 
R-APS messages received are not forwarded
GT value should be greater than the maximum expected forwarding delay time that takes one R-
APS message to circulate around the ring.  This  prevents loops within the ring.

<<<PAGE 454>>>
R-APS Messages
When the RPL owner receives the R-APS (NR) message, it starts the Wait-To-
Restore (WTR) timer
The R-APS (NR) message indicates that the ring protection is no longer required
WTR is a timer that must elapse before the RPL owner sets the RPL port to block
Once the WTR timer expires, the RPL 
owner will block the RPL port and 
transmit the R-APS (NR,RB) message 
indicating the RPL is blocked Root 
Blocked (RB)
All ring nodes receive the R-APS (NR,RB) 
message and flush the dynamic MAC 
Addresses learned on their ring ports and 
unblock any previously blocked ports
The ring is now operating in idle mode.

<<<PAGE 457>>>
Virtual Channel
Main ring and each of the sub-rings leaning on the shared link should not be 
part of the same ERP instance, i.e. nodes in these rings should be configured 
with different ERP group id
Virtual channel is the configuration attached to the interconnecting links within 
the sub-rings ERP instances only
ERP v2 supports two implementation options for R-APS control channel of the 
sub-ring
Virtual channel link is defined for sub rings only while the main ring treats it as a 
regular link
Administrators have the option to enable or disable virtual 
channel
By default R-APS virtual channel is enabled
-> erp-ring 3 virtual-channel [enable|disable]

<<<PAGE 458>>>
With Virtual Channel
R-APS messages are encapsulated and transmitted over an R-APS Virtual channel 
configured on the major ring
Without Virtual Channel
R-APS messages are terminated at the interconnection nodes but not blocked at RPL 
of the sub-ring
Blocked ports (e.g. RPL) will only block data channel, not the R-APS channel
Prevent segmentation of the R-APS channel

- This gives you the configured STP parameters of VLAN 1. Notice the mode, it’s Per VLAN or 1X1, meaning 
each VLAN runs a separate STP. Additionally, take note of the Bridge ID and the Designated Root. If 
they’re the same then your switch is the Root Bridge for VLAN 1.  
- Is your switch the root?  
 
- If not, where is the root located? 
 
- In the screen capture above, this switch is not the root. The root in this example is a cost of 4 away on 
port 1/1/4. Since we know that Gigabit Ethernet, by default, has a path cost of 4 we can deduct that the 
Root Bridge is the upstream neighbor on that port. If the path cost was 8, we could deduct that the root 
bridge was 2 hops away.  
- We can also deduct from the above output that our STP is relatively stable, it has been 12 hours since the 
last topology change (Topology Age) and we have only had 2 Topology changes 
 
- By default, the bridge priority is 32768 (0x8000). Since all priorities are identical by default, the switch 
with the lowest MAC address is selected as the root bridge.

 4 
1x1 Spanning Tree Mode 
- By default, omniswitch works in 1x1 or Per Vlan Spanning Tree mode. That means there’s a separate 
instance of Spanning Tree for each VLAN. 
- But of course, as default parameters are the same for each VLAN (base MAC address, cost links, etc…), the 
status of each port are the same for each VLAN. To take benefits of 1x1 STP and provide load-balancing, it 
may be necessary to modify bridge priority to have a predictable behavior. 
- As example, this design has greater performance : 
 
- Here, the 6450-B is the Access switch and 6860s are core switches. The 6450-B has a dual attachment to 
the core network to provide redundancy. The goal is to have the linkagg between 6860s always up, and 
one of the uplink up for VLAN 20 and the other one for VLAN 30. 
- To achieve this, simply ensure that 6860-A is root bridge for VLAN 20 and 6860-B root bridge for VLAN 30. 
- By default, each bridge has a priority of 32768, putting a lower value will give it better priority to become 
root bridge : 
6860-A -> spantree vlan 20 priority 20000 
6860-B -> spantree vlan 30 priority 20000
